title: Shortest Run Reaching a Total
statement:
You get a positive integer target and an array nums of positive integers.

Find the shortest contiguous run of nums whose sum is at least target (it does not have to hit it exactly). Return its length, or 0 if even the whole array falls short.

examples.why: No two neighbours reach 9 (the best pair is 2 + 4 = 6). The run 5, 2, 4 sums to 11.
No run sums to exactly 7, but 4 + 4 = 8 is at least 7, and that counts.
The whole array only sums to 12.

hints: Every number is positive. What does that tell you about the sum when a run grows to the right, or shrinks from the left?
Fix the right end. The best left end is the furthest-right one that still keeps the sum at or above the target. As the right end moves on, can that left end ever move back?
Keep a window and its sum. Add the next number on the right; then, while the sum is still at least the target, record the length and drop the leftmost number.

explain.intuition:
Because every number is positive, a longer run always has a bigger sum. So once a window reaches the target, the only useful move is to shrink it from the left to see how short it can get. And when you then extend the right end, the left end never needs to move back: a window starting further left would only be longer.

That makes both ends move only forward. Each index enters the window once and leaves it once, so the whole scan is linear. Think of it like a debounce window that only ever slides forward: you never revisit old events.
steps: While sum ≥ target: update best with right − left + 1, subtract nums[left] and move left forward.
After the loop, return best, or 0 if it never changed.
pitfalls: Looking for an exact sum. The rule is at least the target, so [4, 4] with target 7 gives 2, not 0.
Using if instead of while for shrinking. One new large number can let you drop several small ones on the left.
Returning Infinity (or a sentinel like n + 1) when no run qualifies. The answer then is 0.

solutions.title: Grow a run from every start
solutions.idea: For each start, add numbers to the right until the sum reaches the target, and keep the shortest length found.

solutions.title: Prefix sums + binary search
solutions.idea: Prefix sums are strictly increasing because the numbers are positive. For each start i, binary-search the first prefix that is at least prefix[i] + target.

solutions.title: Sliding window
solutions.idea: Extend on the right; while the window still reaches the target, record it and shrink from the left. Both ends only move forward.

followups: What breaks if the numbers can be negative or zero? Which approach survives? (Hint: a monotonic deque over prefix sums.)
Return the start and end of the shortest run instead of its length. Which one do you pick on a tie?
